A rhythm stuck in a loop
A 4–12 Hz rhythm circulates between brainstem, cerebellum, thalamus and motor cortex, and drives the arm.
Propranolol and primidone help about half of patients. Where they act on this loop is not established.
T-type calcium channels pace the rhythm at these sites. A blocker aims to damp it at the source.
Deep brain stimulation: an electrode in the thalamus interrupts the relay. Adjustable and reversible.
Focused ultrasound: sound beams make a small permanent lesion at the same spot. No incision.
Every treatment targets a point on the loop.
